memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You must therefore make a distinction between clean and unclean animals and between unclean and clean birds. Do not defile yourselves by any animal or bird or anything that moves along the ground — those which I have set apart as unclean for you.'" - Lev 20:25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Back to the food laws of chapter 11, and here God explains their purpose from a different angle: they trained Israel to make distinctions.

Three times a day, at every meal, an Israelite had to think. Is this permitted? Is this set apart? The discipline of discernment was built into breakfast.

Those particular laws no longer bind us. Jesus declared all foods clean (Mark 7:19), and Peter learned it on a rooftop. But the capacity they trained is needed more than ever.

We live surrounded by voices, and many of them sound spiritual. Discernment is not suspicion, and it is not cynicism. It is the trained ability to tell what is true from what merely sounds true.

Hebrews describes it as something developed rather than downloaded: solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained themselves to distinguish good from evil (Heb 5:14). Constant use. It grows through steady time in Scripture, honest prayer, and life alongside believers who help us see clearly.

The alternative is being carried along by whatever is loudest.

What are you doing, practically, to train your discernment?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How are you actively training yourself to tell truth from error?
2. Which voices shape your thinking most at the moment?
3. What would deepen your knowledge of Scripture this year?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, train my heart and mind through Your Word. Give me discernment to tell what is true from what merely sounds true, and keep me from being carried along. Amen.
